en: The Tantra entitled *Śrī-sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījāla-saṃvara*.
Oṃ! Homage to Śrī Vajrasattva!
He who always abides within the secret, supreme, and delightful essence of all things.
The being who consists of all Buddhas is Vajrasattva, the supreme bliss. ||1||
This Blessed One, the Self-Arisen, is the sole supreme deity, the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījālasaṃvara*. (2)
Neither passion nor dispassion is found, nor is a middle way perceived; this is the seal of the illusion of all women—this is the non-dual path of liberation. 3.
Of all illusions, the illusion of a woman is preeminent;
for she is established by her very nature through her power and inherent disposition. 4.
By this [virtue], women attain respect in these three worlds;
even those of ill conduct achieve success through all gains, pleasures, and festivals. (5)
Those perfected through the illusion of all women by means of transformations of their own forms—this is the seal of manifold illusion known as the Ḍākinī, according to the Milicchha tradition. (6)
O Ḍākinī, for traveling through the sky, one who is purified by the Buddha-element attains the accomplishment of moving through all space. 7.
The Universal Seal (viśvamudrā) is [attained] from all sides through the universal vows (saṃvara);
this union with all Buddhas is renowned as the Ḍākinī. 8.
The Buddha-element is conceptualized as moving through the sky;
the accomplishment of going everywhere is the Ḍākinī who is the self of all Buddhas. 9.
That which is renowned as "Sukha" (Bliss) is the Great Bliss (Mahāsukha) of all Buddhas;
through the application of all illusory means, it is the vow (saṃvara), and by that, the vow. 10.
Everywhere, from every source, everything, in every way, at all times, and by itself—he becomes every state of being, both stable and moving, beginning with all the Buddhas. 11.
The being of mind, meditative concentration, and the manifold aspects of the conduct of awakening—being of the very form of the conquerors of Māra—he indeed becomes the awakened one of awakening. 12.
The Vajra and the Holder of the Vajra, likewise the Lotus and the Holder of the Lotus, and the Jewel and the Holder of the Jewel—these indeed constitute their families. 13.
That very passion is dispassion; it becomes both desire and liberation.
It is the three times, the three worlds of existence, the three attachments, the three realms, and the triple world-system.
All that is stationary is indeed he, appearing in various and manifold forms;
all that is moving is the universe from every side, for he becomes everything. 15.
Beginning with these, they are infinite in extent; equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), this [wisdom] becomes all things, as limitless as the realm of space. 16.
The Tathāgata Śrīvajrasattva, who encompasses the entire expanse of space;
the Samvara of the Net of Ḍākinīs, the union of all Buddhas. 17.
By means of this ritual procedure for the mudrās, one attains the state of all-buddhahood in this very life, which otherwise would require tens of millions of incalculable eons.
I shall conceive that which is the self-vow of the essence of all Buddhas;
it is the ultimate means for realizing the self, the self-vow of the essence of all Buddhas. 19.

For those who practice the yoga of the infinite and the finite with respect to the objective support of the deity, the yoga consisting of a reflected image arises in relation to [objects] such as cast [images]. (20)
Through the application of the intention toward reality, one's own yoga directed toward the deity as the focal point becomes the supreme, imperishable self-convention. 21.
Yoga does not arise with respect to reflected images, such as those cast in metal;
rather, through the great yoga of the spirit of enlightenment (bodhicitta), deities manifest for the yogi. 22.
This bodhicitta is the vajra, the very self of all Buddhas;
therefore, through the yoga of the universal self, one attains the state of all Buddhas. 23.
The self indeed is all-buddhahood and all-heroism;
therefore, through union with one's own tutelary deity, one should accomplish the self alone. (24)
By this, the state of all Buddhas, the state of all Sūris, and the state of all Vajradharas are accomplished in this very life. 25.

Thus spoke the Blessed One, Śrī Vajrasattva. This is the first chapter, the Ritual of the Knowledge-Seal (*jñānamudrā*) for entering the sphere of the vision of supreme reality, from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījālasamvara*. 1.
For that Blessed One is Yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, the Samvara of the Net of Ḍākinīs, the Union of All Buddhas. (1)
The union with the nature of Vajrasattva, the penetration of all, is accomplished as the great bliss of the sovereign yoga of the assembly of all Buddhas. (2)
Therefore, through bliss alone, one attains the state of all-buddhahood—the great bliss that is the sovereign power of yoga in the union with all buddhas. (3)
In this [path], there is no impurity, no restrictive rule, no austerity, and no difficult task;
it is accomplished through non-difficult means, without rules, and with ease and joy.
Therefore, he whose activity is directed as he desires, who is all-pervading and omniscient, acts according to his will and dwells just as he does upon the earth. ||5||
Whether standing or sitting, whether engaged in walking meditation or remaining as he was, whether laughing or conversing—wherever and in whatever manner he may be. (6)
Whether one has not entered the maṇḍala or is possessed of all obscurations—even one of little merit attains accomplishment through the yoga of one's own tutelary deity. (7)
Indeed, by means of this yoga of reality, one shall accomplish everything;
for in every way, one is not defiled by bad food or any evil deeds whatsoever. (8)
By means of this procedure for the mudrās, one attains supreme, perfect buddhahood through the sealing [of the body], even if it has been unattainable for millions of eons. ||9||
I shall now explain that supreme means for accomplishing one's own self, the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījālasaṃvara*. (10)

Through the union with the self of Vajrasattva and the manifestation of the descent [of power] as it occurs, one whose nature is the universal mudrā attains accomplishment, even if they possess little merit. (11)
By the mere sealing with this [mudrā], one is empowered by all the Buddhas;
through self-empowerment, the assembly of all the Buddhas truly comes to be. (12)
Through the union with all Buddhas, one becomes composed of all Buddhas;
and by virtue of being composed of all Buddhas, one accomplishes all Buddhas. ||13||
Those who see him as united [with the deity] worship him in every way;
for indeed, when honored through such illustrations, they become all Buddhas. 14.
Indeed, by both seeing and touching this maṇḍala of the Universal Buddha, even those who have not entered it become seers of the truth. 15.
Through seeing and touching, as well as through hearing and remembering, they are liberated from all sins and become endowed with all spiritual accomplishments. ||16||
Indeed, through the unions with all the Buddhas and by means of this [practice] of all the Buddhas, even those who are not noble ones are liberated and they touch the awakening of a Buddha. 17.
Everywhere, from every source, everything, in every way, at all times, and by himself—he beholds his own self as accomplished, consisting of all Buddhas. 18.
Thus abiding within the self of all, the Tathāgatas worship [him] with vast arrays of great clouds of every kind of offering. (19)
Through the yoga of the worship of the self of all, one indeed attains the supreme state of Śrī Vajrasattva, the universal vow (saṃvara) that is the very essence of all Buddhas. 20.
Through the enjoyment of all yogas, the four glorious qualities are accomplished;
for the Blessed One, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, is indeed all yoga. ||21||
Indeed, he experiences the entirety of the three realms without exception, enjoying all yogic enjoyments according to his pleasure. 22.
One should worship one's own self through the yoga of one's own tutelary deity;
indeed, through that yoga, one should worship all the joys of yoga. 23.
And by tasting this himself through intense application, he attains accomplishment;
indeed, by means of this elixir of bliss which is the essence of all Buddhas. 24.
Through the long life, youth, and health of Śrī Vajrasattva, one attains true bliss;
he indeed accomplishes everything everywhere and at all times. 25.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Śrī Vajrasattva: “The Union of All Buddhas, the Net of Dakinis’ Secret Vow.
This concludes the second chapter, the Union of Śrī Vajrasattva, from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinījālasaṃvara*. 2.
For that Blessed One is Yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata,
the *Saṃvara* of the *Ḍākinījāla* through the union of all Buddhas.
He is the glorious union of Śrī-Vajrasattva, the illustrious bliss of his own *samaya*.
The great bliss of the sovereign yoga of the union of all Buddhas. ||2||
By the power of the union with Śrī Vajrasattva alone, all the festivals of the bliss of yoga are spontaneously and perfectly accomplished in every respect. ||3||
By the power of the union with Śrī Vajrasattva alone, all festivals of bliss and all accomplishments are spontaneously realized from every side. (4)
Through the power of the union with Śrī Vajrasattva alone, all the festivals of sovereignty and bliss are spontaneously accomplished in every respect. (5)
By the power of the union with Śrī Vajrasattva alone, supreme women arise everywhere, as far as the limits of the realm of space. (6)
For him, those beloved ones arise from the samaya, following his own samaya;
they are the supreme samayas of Abhiyoga, Mahāyoga, and Sarvātma. ||7||
And for her who wanders alone, there are beloved companions who move along with her;
she is the supremely radiant Ḍākinī of the Union of All Buddhas. 8.
Through universal delights in every way, all mudrās are great bliss;
all offerings belong to the supreme King, the goddesses who are supremely eternal. (9)
Through union with Śrī Vajrasattva and the assemblies of all goddesses, one who is everywhere auspicious throughout the universe attains happiness and the corresponding accomplishment. 10.
By this very sealing alone, all the goddesses of great bliss, whose presiding deity is Vajrasattva and who extend to the limits of the realm of space, [are sealed]. (11)
Men, too, who possess the strength of passion, enjoy themselves, delighting one another with all the festivals of the pleasure of union. 12.
And they worship with the emanations of all their own bodies and all their sense organs, through the spreading and gathering of vast arrays of great clouds of every kind of offering. (13)
Delighted, they serve [the Buddhas] with all kinds of jewels and with those things consisting of the bliss of all yogas, which have issued forth from the joy of the Dharma. (14)
Being served by the enjoyments of all goddesses according to one's pleasure, one should worship one's own self through the yoga of its presiding deity. 15.
Worshipping through the internal yoga all the joys of yoga,
and impelling himself by means of the yoga of his own intellect, he attains perfection.
By means of this elixir of bliss which is the essence of all Buddhas, one attains the true happiness of long life, youth, health, and well-being as Śrī Vajrasattva. 17.
The great body of all Buddhas, the eloquence of all Buddhas, the great mind of all Buddhas, the great festival of all Buddhas. ||18||
The great king of all Buddhas, the sovereign lord of all Vajra-holders, the lord of all world-protectors, the sovereign lord of all jewels. (19)
Being perfumed by them, he who desires to fly up falls;
yet, as a great Siddha of all the goddesses, he becomes a renowned universal monarch (cakravartin). 20.

There are no such noble boons as these, for they are equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), as limitless as the realm of space (ākāśadhātu), and constitute a festival of blissful sovereignty over all things. (21)
By which all the vehicles are accomplished for him in this very life in every respect—the sovereignty of the union with all Buddhas and great bliss. (22)
There are no such noble boons as those, which are equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) and equal to it;
they extend to the limits of the realm of space and consist of the festival of the bliss of all sovereignty. 23.
By means of the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga*, the *Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*, and so forth, his vehicles will be accomplished in every way in this very life. (24)
Thus spoke the Blessed One, Śrī Vajrasattva, from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinījālasaṃvara*, the third section: the *Śrīvajrasamayakalpa* on the auspicious union with all goddesses. 3.
For that Blessed One is Yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījālasaṃvara*. (1)
The supreme fortunate one, the bow of the union with all goddesses;
the intense union through the savoring of bliss, the firm and eternal Manmatha. ||2||
He enjoys the great forms, sounds, and delightful flavors of all Buddhas, as well as the pleasant touches of all Buddhas, through these sensory enjoyments. 3.
The Buddhists have perfected the perfections, the dhāraṇīs, and likewise the stages; how much more, then, do these fortunate ones delight in the divine and the human? 4.
One personally realizes the Buddha-enlightenment, which is difficult for us to achieve, which is perfected, which is great bliss, and which is most fortunate through the taste of happiness. ||5||
He enjoys the glory arising from all accomplishments, belonging to all the Tathāgatas, and the fortune of all enjoyments through those very enjoyments. 6.
Having snatched away the supreme accomplishment of the Vajrins, the supreme glory of Lokeśa, and the supreme bliss of the Buddhas, he enjoys them for himself. ||7||
Having forcibly seized the great sovereignty of all Buddhas throughout the three realms without exception, he enjoys it through his own manly power. (8)
When he has fully manifested and enjoys the supreme sovereignty and liberation—the great siddhi of all Buddhas—what need is there to mention other splendors? ||9||
Having forcibly seized from Nārāyaṇa stable fortune (Lakṣmī), from Hara spiritual perfection (Siddhi), and from Smara the goddess Rati, he bestows them upon his devotees. ||10||
Having manifested the unsurpassed, supreme sovereignty belonging to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, she bestows it upon these [women]; what need is there to mention her other glories? 11.
There is nothing that she cannot bestow, nor is there anything she will not do;
she grants and performs all the activities of all the Buddhas. 12.
Having taken away even the state of Buddhahood from a bodhisattva, he gives it back; how much more so other accomplishments, the foremost rites, and their various manifestations? (13)
Having accomplished the unfailing expansion, the destroyer of all armies, the universal monarch who is the great accomplishment of all Buddhas becomes renowned. 14.
Through the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*, he manifests the great siddhi of all Buddhas and sets it in motion. 15.
In some places the great mind of enlightenment, in others the conduct as it truly is;
and in some places the supreme descent from the Tuṣita gods. ||16||
In some places there is indeed the purity of birth; in some, the departure from the city;
in some, the great night of enlightenment; and in some, the defeat of Māra. (17)
In some places there is the perfect awakening to enlightenment; in some, the turning of the wheel [of Dharma];
and in others, the suppression by means of the Dharma of those who are terrified of others. 18.

In some places, there is the sovereignty over all accomplishments, the glorious *Trilokavijaya*; and in others, the unsurpassed power of the perfected ones (*siddha*) according to the foremost of all ritual manuals (*kalpa*). 19.

In this way, through the infinite and supreme vows that embody the essence of all Buddhas, he dances with the miraculous transformations of the playful sport of delighting in the means of discipline. (20)
Possessing the supreme great accomplishment, he is a steadfast lord of great sovereignty, endowed with beauty, longevity, strength, complexion, and splendor, like another Vajrasattva. (21)
Being served and likewise worshipped by the Tathāgatas, the glorious Vajrasattva, the lord of all goddesses and the benefactor of the world, attains perfection. 22.
Having sealed the entire realm of sentient beings in manifold ways, he bestowed upon the Bodhisattvas that firm, immortal, and difficult-to-attain [perfection]. (23)
He himself becomes all the kalpas, both without remainder and with remainder;
he acts through the vows of the essence of all Buddhas, born from the yoga of awakening. 24.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śrī Vajrasattva, from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyogadākinījālasaṃvara*. (25)
The fourth [chapter], the Śrī-samayakalpa named Sarvatoviśvasubhagottamasiddhi. ||4||
For that Blessed One is the Yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*. (1)
For he alone is truly perfected, directed according to his will;
in all ritual procedures, he possesses the supreme, unsurpassed accomplishment. (2)
For the sake of disciplining sentient beings who desire various methods through their engagement in diverse karmas, and for the attainment of all happiness. ||3||
That very Blessed One is Yoga, the miraculous manifestation of all Buddhas;
manifesting for the sake of all sentient beings, he is most swiftly accomplished. ||4||
One should perform the dance according to the Buddha-vows, whether daily, monthly, or annually, or even according to the specific occasion. 5.
Or likewise, [it may be] composed of all the elements or of the root of life;
it is accomplished by means of the faces of one's own tutelary deity and the application of mudrās. ||6||
Whatever is offered in the maṇḍala as a universal mudrā-oblation, all the groups of disciples should worship that very thing and offer it. ||7||
Henceforth I shall proclaim the miraculous manifestation of all Buddhas, as it occurs through the narrative of every eon according to its appropriate manifestation. (8)
Abiding eternally within the supreme, most delightful secret, which is the self of all, the being who consists of all Buddhas is Vajrasattva, the ultimate bliss. 9.
For that Blessed One is Yoga—stable, supremely eternal, ever-present, and indeed his very nature, which is difficult to transcend. || 10 ||
Through the application of various karmas, for those who desire various ritual methods, the Buddhas, Vajradharas, and others are known to have been created as means of discipline. ||11||
This becomes all phenomena, both stable and moving, beginning with all the Buddhas;
it is the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*. 12.
By this application of illusion, the supreme universe is everywhere accomplished through the disciplines of the Buddhas and others for the highest benefit of all sentient beings. 13.
The Consolation of Śrī Vajrasattva.
In the past, in a former age, during the teaching of the great-souled Tathāgata Śāśvata, there once existed the established order of the world.
At that time, all sentient beings became endowed with absolute emptiness;
through their union with the nature of cessation, they were ceased and completely extinguished. 15.
That very Blessed One, the yoga of Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, enters into the nirvāṇa of the Buddhas for the sake of the purification of all liberation. 16.
Neither non-empty nor empty, the Middle Way is not apprehended;
through the yoga of the perfection of wisdom, it is the means [attained] by one whose nature is compassion. 17.

Then, while manifesting the perfections of compassion, skillful means, and wisdom, he conceptualizes all conceptualization even within non-conceptual resolute belief; and amidst all phenomena that are free from conceptualization, he conceptualizes for the sake of the welfare of sentient beings. (18)
That voice of Dharma was like an echo;
then, through the extensive expansions of the true qualities of the Great Mahāyāna, all the Tathāgatas of the three times were sung in the three samayas. 19.

Unshakable, possessing the nature of universal essence, compassionate by nature, they are the removers of the world's suffering; bestowers of the accomplishment of all infinite virtues, stainless and immovable, they possess the supreme dharma of equanimity. There is no comparison for them with space, even for a mere atom of a fraction of their qualities, which are limitless and manifest for all beings.

Among those who bestow the accomplishment of the supreme element, who are beyond comparison, and who possess peerless success, there is a constant, stainless compassion that has arisen for those lost in darkness; the fulfillment of their vows is the nature of non-obstruction. Devoted to accomplishing the welfare of the world, this all-pervading wisdom constantly shines forth for those whose very essence is great compassion; for it is not subject to obstruction.

The immovable practice of compassion proceeds, bestowing the supreme accomplishment of the three worlds. Oh, how wonderful is the nature of the sublime Dharma, that even when the Amitābhas have reached their final consummation and passed into the blissful state, they remain so! May those who have attained the supreme goal through the granting of boons always grant me the supreme accomplishment of the Three Samayas, throughout all the three worlds.
The Lords who bestow the supreme accomplishment are those whose course is the three times; they are beyond being conceptualized.
For this is the full extent of the truly existent qualities of all Buddhas;
indeed, even when uttered but once, it bestows the state of all-buddhahood. 20.
By means of this king of hymns, through the yoga of the essence of all Buddhas, all Victors of the three times are accomplished by the three pledges. ||21||
And they show him their own forms, all of which are truly wonderful to behold; they offer cries of "Well done! and bestow perfected boons.
All self-attainments are delightful and fulfill all aspirations;
they bestow the supreme yoga, the highest state of Buddhahood. 23.
Now I shall describe its method of accomplishment, which brings about eternal success;
by means of which one attains eternal success even in this very life. (24)
One should perform the assembly of all Buddhas through the releasing of the vajra-claps;
through the assemblies of the *sampātāla* beats, one should apply the triple beat (*tritāla*). || 25 ||
Whatever sense faculty should proceed along the path, one should carry it as consisting of all Buddhas by its very nature through the yoga of non-concentration. 26.
Just as one is eager with songs sung by various singers and melodies,
so too should one recite everything everywhere, or indeed recite it immeasurably.

Seeing everywhere, from all sides, everything, in every way, at all times, and by himself—that which is accomplished as consisting of all Buddhas—the excellent practitioner attains accomplishment. 28.
By this, both the state of all Buddhas and the state of all Sūris, as well as the state of all Vajradharas, is accomplished in this very life. (29)

By reciting this supreme king of hymns, the extensive praise of all the qualities of the Buddhas, one attains in a single moment the all-pervading, eternal accomplishment of yoga and imperishable bliss. (30)

By this king of hymns, indeed, [one propitiates] the Lord who consists of the self of all, who disciplines the entire universe in every way, and who is the Tathāgata of all things in every respect. 31.

Then, by means of the three pledges and so forth, which are unsurpassed among all conceptualizations, the realm of sentient beings as limitless as the expanse of space is liberated. Thus [it is said].
The Consolation of Śrī Vairocana.
In the past, in a former age, during the teaching of the Great-souled Tathāgata Śāśvata, there first arose the stability of the world.
At that time, all sentient beings became exceedingly wicked and fiercely violent;
due to their extreme wickedness and ferocity, they fell again into the Raurava hell.
Then, having passed away from there, all those beings were joined together once more through the power of karmic connection.
They became exceedingly more wicked due to the empowerments and accomplishments of Māra:
fevers, poisons, planetary afflictions, diseases, the disturbances of ḍākinīs, plagues, as well as Māras and Vināyakas, who became most extremely malevolent. (35)

They destroy the three worlds and devour the practitioners; they terrify the gods and others, and they cause the sacred teachings to perish. Thereupon, the gods, together with Indra, approached Brahmā.
Brahmā and the gods, including Indra, sought refuge with Viṣṇu;
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the gods approached Mahādeva;
and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara sought refuge with the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra). || 37 ||
Then the Blessed One, the Vajra-holder, by means of the vajra-clapping mudrā and through the yoga of Śrī Vajrasattva, should assemble all the Buddhas. (38)
With his two arms, by means of the vajra-bind and the release of the vajra-snap, he who is the self of the yoga of Śrī Vajrasattva shall assemble all the Buddhas. (39)
At the mere command of this [deity], the assemblies of all the Buddhas arrive in their multitudes, trembling with awe; what need then to speak of those who follow the path? 40.
By means of the liberations of the vajra-snap, all world-systems without exception are filled with all the Buddhas together with their Vajra-holders, like a heap of sesame seeds. (41)
Gentleness is not effective toward those who are extremely wicked and fierce;
all the Tathāgatas possess a wheel of wrath consisting of wisdom and skillful means. 42.
The fury of those possessed by anger has the nature of incinerating even the three worlds;
how much more so the entire triple realm of all the Buddhas? 43.
Then, having firmly fixed the mind upon the tips of the nostrils, those who have conquered their senses spoke of the yoga of mudrā, characterized by long and hot exhalations from the nose. ||44||
That very Blessed One, the Yoga, emitting Vajrakrodha, is the glorious Heruka, the Great Vajra, blazing like the dissolution of the world from his secret organ. 45.
The being consists of blue flames, with a mandala shining with red flames, like another fire of the great cremation ground at the time of the final dissolution. 46.
With blazing hair and great flames, and fierce with a skull-diadem, he was as terrifying as a cremation ground at the onset of the great dissolution. 47.
With the various movements of his faces, variegated by the combination of the Furious and other rasas, he danced with a radiant gaze accompanied by playful arching brows and frowns. ||48||
Having set ablaze the three worlds—including Rudra, Indra, Upendra, along with Candra, Ārka, Yama, and Aṃśaka—one should reduce them to ashes at the time of dissolution. 49.
Having brought about possession by means of the sounds of the bell and the rattling of the vajra-adorned khaṭvāṅga, he can once again restore to life even all that has been turned to ashes. 50.
From him were produced most terrifying shadows born of the blazing sun, created capable of devouring the blood from the mouths of all wicked beings, such as Māra and his like. (51)
Accompanied by them, that king wanders through the cremation ground;
he is Vajra, blazing with the maṇḍala of Ḍākinīs through the union with Vajra. (52)

Having thoroughly purified the realm of sentient beings who are extremely wicked and fierce, one should indeed establish those who are purified in enlightenment as a Buddha within pure Buddha-fields. ||53||
"By means of all the unsurpassed tantras, such as the Śrīvajrakāma and Krodha, the realm of sentient beings, as limitless as the expanse of space, has been perfected. (54) Thus it is said.
The Consolation of Śrī Heruka.
In the past, in ages long gone by, during the teaching of the Great-Souled Tathāgata Śāśvata, there once existed this condition of the world.
At that time, all sentient beings became established in wrong views; due to their extremely perverted vision, they fell into the Mahāraurava hell. 56.
That very Blessed One is the yoga for the purification of the bodhicitta;
the yoga consisting of ruby is established in Vajradharma. ||57||
Just as this red [lotus] is not defiled by the faults of passion, so too, through the mere contemplation of it, the Victors attain the state of Supreme Lord;
thus the glorious Avalokiteśvara is Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata. (58)
Through the purification of all passion, the Blessed One, the supreme bestower of boons, [acts] by means of various methods of discipline and various festivals of discipline. 59.
Avalokiteśvara shall become the king Padmanarteśvara, through the union with Padmajāla and the Samvara of the Ḍākinījāla. ||60||
"By means of the supreme *sarvakalpas* beginning with Śrī Padmanarteśvara, the realm of sentient beings has been purified throughout the entirety of the expanse of space. (61) Thus it is said.
The Consolation of the Glorious Padmanarteśvara.
In the past, in times long gone, during the teaching of the great-souled Tathāgata Śāśvata, there once existed a state of stability for the world.
At that time, all beings became exceedingly wicked and greedy;
due to their extreme avarice, they fell into hell along with their ancestors.
Falling from there once again, they encountered great poverty and, afflicted by the miseries of hunger, thirst, and the like, sought to devour one another. (64)
That very Blessed One is Yoga, the ultimate reality, the great treasure;
for the sake of purifying those who are extremely corrupt, he becomes Vajrasūrya and the others. (65)
Ākāśagarbha fulfills all hopes; he is the fulfiller of every aspiration.
He rains down all manner of jewels, such as the precious gems of celestial maidens and the like. 66.
Gentleness is of no avail toward those who are utterly wicked and fierce;
rather, it is the heat of the sun, consisting of wisdom and skillful means, that accomplishes everything.
By means of instruments, obstructions, and especially by means of withdrawals,
having conquered the performance of all purposes, he shall withdraw the three worlds.
"By means of the supreme *sarvakalpa* rituals, beginning with the *Trilokavijaya*, the realm of sentient beings, as limitless as the expanse of space, has been liberated. (69) Thus it is said.
The Glorious Vajrasūryaśvāsa.
In the past, in times long gone, during the teaching of the great-souled Tathāgata Śāśvata, there once existed this state of the world.
At that time, all sentient beings became utterly devoid of vigor;
due to this utter lack of vigor, they fell into the Avīci hell. (71)
That very Blessed One, the yoga of Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, became the non-dual Śrī Paramāśva (the Glorious Supreme Horse) through the purification of Haṭhayoga. 72.
Through the resolute conviction (*adhimokṣa*) in universal purity, he possesses the power of non-attachment (*prasajya-bala-māna*);
then, by means of the five awakened weapons, he shall conquer all worlds. 73.
Having conquered all worlds by means of your prowess and treading upon them,
crushing the realm of sentient beings— which is exceedingly wicked, fierce, and foremost— in many ways,
you must completely purify everything through other emanations of yourself.
Through deceit and even through violence, he becomes addicted to force and pride. || 74 ||
The power established in the world of the moving and the unmoving...
Constantly protecting his own kingdom through various means of discipline.
For those who are lustful, there shall be desire; for the fierce, the highest ferocity;
for the gentle, the supreme gentleness; and for the forceful, firm valor. (76)
Having overstepped the Supreme Lord and become intoxicated by his own power and pride, he has seized Bhīmādevī and enjoys her with various sensual pleasures. 77.
Having summoned Nārāyaṇa and displayed his strength and pride, he summoned Rukmiṇī and enjoyed her with various pleasures. 78.
Having assailed Prajāpati and exerted his power and pride, he has seized the goddess Praśāntī and enjoys her along with her attendants. (79)
Having completely overcome Kāmadeva and exerting his power and pride,
he enjoys pleasure, delight, fortitude, and sovereignty through various sensual gratifications.
Thus, these and others are infinite and boundless, equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) and equal to all;
they are as limitless as the realm of space, possessing the supreme prowess of vajra-activity. (81)
Established in the glorious Vajrasattva within the expanse of all space, they have been accomplished through forceful yoga by means of the practice of policy and human effort. 82.
Having fully attained sovereignty over the three worlds, that wielder of the vajra should accomplish the infinite and supreme bodhicitta through haṭhayoga. 83.
Through the conviction that all is pure, one who possesses the power of non-attachment may, by means of heroic exertion, crush the awakening of the Buddha. ||84||

Having personally attained the immortal, difficult-to-accomplish, perfected, and great bliss of the awakening of a Buddha—the supreme and most eternal state—through his own yoga, he becomes the self of that yoga. 85.
Having sealed the entire realm of sentient beings in manifold ways, he bestowed upon them the firm and immortal enlightenment that is so difficult to attain. 86.
He himself becomes all the eons, both without exception and without remainder;
he accomplishes the welfare of all sentient beings through supreme transformations of ultimate reality. 87.

Then, by means of all the unsurpassed *kalpas*, beginning with the glorious *Paramāśva* and others, the realm of sentient beings as far as the limits of the space-element was fully perfected. (88) Thus [it is said].
The consolation of the glorious Supreme Horse.
These and other such self-arisen mudrās of discourse are infinite in extent, equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), and as limitless as the realm of space. 89.
The entire expanse of space shines forth, established within Śrī Vajrasattva;
they attain meditative absorption through the perfections of the sovereignty and accomplishments of the self-nature of all. 90.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śrī-Vajrasattva, from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*, the fifth chapter on the Knowledge Ritual of the Narrative Mudrās. 5.
Hereafter, I shall proclaim the supreme universal mandala, the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījālasaṃvara*. 1.
In the supreme and most delightful secret, there is the perpetual abiding in the self of all;
it is the blissful arising of the glorious Vajrasattva, who consists of all Buddhas. 2.
Adorned with the great divine jewel-kings of the Tathāgatas and other ornaments, with excellent canopies spread above and bells suspended from auspicious banners; ||3||

Accompanied by the miraculous displays of vajra songs, offerings, and so forth, as well as dance and instrumental music, and provided with the application of flowers, incense, lamps, and the like. ||4||
Or again, they bring delight to the world in their own gardens and other such places through the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījālasamvara*. 5.
Having established the seat there, its surface is characterized by a soft touch;
for that is indeed the seat of universal purity, veiled by the cloth of the universal lotus.
Indeed, the deity Śrīvajrasattva manifests transformations wherever there are the miraculous displays of the sovereign power of yoga from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga*. (7)
And everywhere there is his own seat, according to its foundation:
square, with four doors, and provided with door-keepers. ||8||
One should visualize the Gaṇamaṇḍala, with women beautifully adorned facing their respective presiding deities, and graced by the marks of their own mudrās. 9.
Human blood, when processed, is known as *mahārakta*;
it is beneficial by its very nature, perfected through its own power and inherent quality. (10)
Vajra-water, together with the vajra and consecrated with great blood, becomes even more effective through its power; one should place it in a lotus vessel. ||11||
The Blessed One is indeed Great Passion, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata;
he is the adamantine heart of all Buddhas, the commitment that is difficult to transgress. (12)
Because it is not obstructed and is accomplished through his great blood, and because it arises from great passion (mahārāga), it is known as "great red" (mahārakta). ||13||
Greatly red, with camphor and mixed with red sandalwood, established in the midst of the Gaṇas, it is the glorious elixir that dwells within all. 14.
One who possesses the yoga of the self as the presiding deity, tasting [the nectar] with the ring finger and thumb like the drinking of soma, attains eternal perfection. 15.
By means of this elixir of bliss which is the very essence of all Buddhas, one attains the true happiness of the accomplished Śrī Vajrasattva—longevity, youth, and health. 16.
In this regard, for one who desires to rise up and proceed to the station of the stage, there is the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasamvara*. (17)
Everywhere, from every side, everything, in every way, and at all times, he himself becomes all things—both the stable and the moving—everywhere, beginning with the Buddhas. 18.
Having performed protection by means of this, one becomes like another Śrī Vajrasattva; one attains accomplishment through the commitments of the Ḍākinījāla, which are the essence of all Buddhas. 19.

Then, having bathed, his limbs anointed with fragrant unguents, adorned with various ornaments, clothed in variegated garments, wearing garlands, and rendered sweet-smelling by the offering of perfumes; ||20||

Omnipresent and bringing universal auspiciousness, being raised up (or causing to rise) by means of arrows (or moments), the impelling force is fully manifested through the application of the descent of the silk-banner. ||21||

One is liberated from all sins and perfected by all merits not merely through the sight of the rising of the sun-like moons of the Perfectly Awakened Ones, but through their appearance [in the world]. ||22||
It is joined with the fixed path, adorned with cessation, the "arousing" *dhruva*, perfected, and the blissful one that arouses [the soul] from all sides. 23.

The pledge (samaya), which has transcended the state of space through the arising of existence and non-existence in the supreme yoga of emptiness— may that glorious Sugata, the illustrious Śrī-Vajrasattva, the fortunate one, arouse me as a being. 24.
For this [teaching], when being sung, would raise up again those who have utterly passed into final nirvāṇa and those who are dead; how much more so, then, those subject to rebirth? (25)
Endowed with the four paths, adorned with liberation, characterized by universal trust (and likewise), perfected, it is the means for accomplishing the realms of Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ. ||26||
Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ, saluted by Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ;
Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ, the giver of prosperity to Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ; Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ, grant me accomplishment! 27.
The union with Śrī Vajrasattva, through the assemblies of all goddesses, becomes the universal Aralli, auspicious in every respect, and is fully accomplished. || 28 ||
Extending to the limits of the realm of space, it is a festival of bliss for all goddesses;
the glorious Vajrasattva is the manifest rising of the full moon and sun. (29)
The *Śrīvajrasattvasaṃyogadākinīsaṃvarodaya* is that which, when perceived even once, gives rise to the bliss of all accomplishments. 30.
Singing with swift and gentle melodies, one should accomplish the universal being by means of the *utthāpanī*, *dhruvā*, *siddhā*, and *viśvāsāritaka* modes of the Gandharva [song]. 31.
Then, one should exhort Śrī Vajrasattva, who is oneself, through this song, as he is deluded regarding all liberation by means of the supreme reality. 32.
Indeed, he is clearly honored with many various delights of passion by means of the great purities of the lotuses, and with the blissful yogas of the supreme eternal. 33.
Having accomplished bliss, he is composed of supreme bliss; he is the supreme bliss, fortunate through the intense union with supreme bliss. ||34||
O Rama, O Ramanah, Hoḥ! You are the faultless and eternal self-samaya.
O self-samaya, you are the supreme goddesses of the highest secret, presiding over the supreme secret. ||35||

The manifest canvas for the discipline of the world with its various and manifold continuities; the source of all stable and moving phenomena; consisting of all phenomena; through the yoga of the essence of all Victors, the blissful *ḍākinī*-net;
O Great Mirror, for the sake of accomplishment! O supreme, eternal accomplishment! *Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ saṃvarya hoḥ*.
Sukhoddharavikurva HŪṂ! It illuminates: A LA LA LA LA LA HOḤ (HO)! Disciple, sit down amidst the variegated nets of Ḍākinīs of all the Tathāgatas!
For this King of Songs is indeed established in Śrī Vajrasattva, through the nets and vows that are everywhere complete and entirely without exception for the sake of all accomplishments. (36)
By means of this being sung, the entire universal mandala displays the miraculous transformations of all Buddhas, without exception or remainder. 37.
O you who are skilled in disciplining all sentient beings, without exception, through the various successions of passion;

O you who manifest the magical transformations of the net of all Tathāgatas by means of the nets of all vows—by that, *hūṃ* to you! O you who are skilled in disciplining all sentient beings, without exception, through the various successions of the gods.
Through the nets of the miraculous manifestations of the net of all Tathāgatas, and through the nets of all vows; *hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ*!

By those who are skilled in the discipline of all beings—without exception or remainder—through the continuous succession of many various fierce [deities]; by the nets of all Tathāgatas, through the miraculous manifestations of the net of all vows; *hūṃ ruluru lubhyoḥ hūṃ*! O you who possess many various lives!

O you who are skilled in the discipline of all sentient beings without exception through your continuity; O you who manifest through the nets of all Tathāgatas and the nets of all vows—HŪṂ! Enter the disciple, HŪṂ! Such mantras as these are infinite and supreme, equal to the entire expanse of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
The songs and mudrās of the Self-Existent One are as limitless as the realm of space. || 38 ||

Established within the glorious Vajrasattva in the expanse of all space, they are endowed with the sovereignty and the attainment of the perfection of all beings through the peace of meditative absorption. (39)
When these [mantras] are sung, all those impelled by the goddesses achieve success through the *samvara* of the *ḍākinījāla*, which is the self of all Buddhas;
and they worship with that which has issued forth from all their own senses. 40.

Through the spreading and accumulation of arrays of great clouds of all offerings, one achieves success by means of forms whose nature consists of the entirety of all phenomena, without exception. 41.
Indeed, even a woman, having entered into the Samaya of the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga* and the *Ḍākinījālasamvara*, may teach by means of the guise of a mudrā. 42.
Indeed, the yoginīs bearing their own vajra symbols manifest, empowered by the face-to-face blessing of their respective presiding deities, and are thus praised. 43.
Through the miraculous displays of music, dance, and song never before heard, and through festivals of bliss consisting of divine forms, sounds, fragrances, tastes, and touches; ||44||
They behold and worship themselves as their own presiding deity;
the most fortunate lover, through the union of divine worship, indeed brings about everywhere the bliss that is auspicious for the entire universe. 45.
Indeed, through the empowerment of the Buddha-net, all the blisses of the accomplishments of the union with Śrī Vajrasattva arise within the maṇḍala.
By the power of the union with Śrī Vajrasattva alone, [this occurs] in every respect. ||46||
He becomes accomplished everywhere through the very bliss that is universally auspicious;
by means of the pleasures consisting of the essence of the sounds and forms of the great bodies of all Buddhas, he worships while beholding himself as the glorious Vajrasattva. 47.

The supreme lover, the most fortunate one through the union of all worship, [is endowed] with the accomplishments of all Buddhas—the self-nature of all Buddhas—without exception or remainder for the sake of the perfected ones. 48.
Through the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga*, the *Ḍākinījālasamvara*, and the dances of the essence of all Buddhas, the Supreme One is seen manifesting his miraculous transformations. (49)
Then, with the four women through the reality of their own secret [mudrās], one should present all offerings by means of the gift of dance and song. (50)
One should cause the deities to bestow gifts upon the assembly. Oṃ hrīḥ haṃ haḥ paramatathāgatasiddha draṃ uṃ ūṃ hūṃ. 2.
O supreme samaya of the great siddhas! O all-pervading great mahāsiddha! draṃ uṃ ūṃ hūṃ. 2.
For this mudrā of song is established in Śrī Vajrasattva; it is worshipped in all ritual activities involving the expansion of worship, whether they be exhaustive or non-exhaustive. (51)
For one whose success does not occur and whose worship does not flourish, all worship becomes perfectly accomplished when performed with this mudrā. 52.
Having performed worship with flowers and other offerings by means of this yoga of worship together with the four women, he should cause all the disciples to enter. ||53||
And those who do not dance, as well as those desiring the accomplishment of their wishes according to their desire, one should cause to enter with their faces covered by various garments. 54.
One should cause the disciples to cast flowers so that they may attain their desired success; upon whichever divine [deity] the flower falls, that deity shall grant him accomplishment. 55.
Then, having opened the mouth and taken hold of the excellent right [hand], one should duly perform the consecration with the jewel of the Buddha. 56.
Deep red, with camphor and mixed with red sandalwood, may he be established in the midst of the Gaṇas, bearing his own vajra as the left-hand emblem. 57.
Endowed with the yoga of one's own tutelary deity, by tasting [the nectar] with the mouths of the ring finger and the thumb as if drinking soma, one attains eternal perfection. 58.
He shall be one who is not to be sealed, not to be gladdened, and not to be consumed, even by the hosts of ḍākinīs from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga*. 59.
Then, having abandoned that illusory form (yathāmaya), he should bestow the commitment of the pledge (samayasamvara),
which is the supreme and eternal command received from all the Buddhas.
Indeed, as many as all the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas who possess the vajra,
the deities, humans, and likewise the virtuous yogins— 61.
If one should transgress the samvara of the union of all Buddhas, one should drink from Bhava's heart that milk which is intensely red. 62.
For the sake of the entire realm of sentient beings and for ultimate purification, one should always practice by means of the yoga of the unceasing nature of phenomena. (63)
One should not abandon one's own self nor afflict it with austerities;
rather, remaining at ease, one should maintain that which is well-awakened within the mind as happiness.
Delight in all yogic enjoyments, for you are free from fear.
"Do not fear; there is no sin for you, for the covenant is inviolable."
The practice of one who wanders alone is perfected, yet the companion is the one who moves together;
by always serving according to the true reality, the unsurpassed enlightenment of a Buddha is attained. //65//
Thus spoke, that is, made known, the glorious Tathāgata Vajrasattva;
he, the wielder of the vajra, commands all the Buddhas who have attained perfect accomplishment. 65.

The knowledge of mudrās is itself the mudrā; one should bestow it upon the disciples for their happiness, together with the yoga and its secrets, through the manifestation of spiritual possession. 66.
From that time forth, by means of the compendium of the knowledge of mudrās, the true disciple attains accomplishment as another Vairocana, the essence of all Buddhas. 67.
Then, having honored the Lord with offerings of food, drink, dance, song, music, and other gifts,
and having fanned Him, once He has been sent forth, they should worship the Great Guru Vajra and others as they please.
Then, having himself entered [the mandala] established by all the Ācāryas...
One should indeed practice both Dharma and truth through the manifestation of one's own entrance [into the state]. ||68||
The domain of Śrī Vajrasattva accomplishes all ritual procedures;
because they are employed in all rituals by their very nature, they are most supreme. (69)
Through the application of various karmas, for the sake of disciplining sentient beings whose natures require diverse means of training, other domains are prescribed. (70)
That very Blessed One, the yoga of Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, arises as the essence of liberation for the sake of purifying all liberations. (71)
Through the mudrā of the empowerment and absorption facing one's own chosen deity, one should bring about the emanation of a Buddha according to the respective mudrā. ||72||
Furthermore, the Blessed One, the supreme Yoga, the lord of all yogins, becomes the arising of the Vajraratna for the sake of purifying those who hate the samaya. (73)
Furthermore, when there is excessive practice, the fortunate one becomes the supreme unchanging;
for the sake of purifying the lotus of the universe, there arises the manifestation of a network of lotuses. (74)
Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Yoga, the Great Jewel of All Space, becomes Śrīvajrasūrya and the others for the sake of the purity of the ultimate truth. 75.
O Blessed One, that very yoga, the prowess of Hayagrīva, becomes the impelling force of the Supreme Horse for the sake of purifying Haṭhayoga. (76)
Even through the empowerment that faces one's own deity, the yoga consisting of a reflected image should be made to dance by means of the yoga of the mudrā. //77//
In this way, through the universal commitment (*viśvasamaya*) to all things, play is accomplished;
[this is] the *Sarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinījālasamvara*. 78.
Everywhere, from every source, and as everything in its entirety, at all times, he himself becomes all things—both the stable and the moving—beginning with all the Buddhas. 79.
Everywhere, through the miraculous transformations of all the Buddhas, he displays his own self by means of assemblies with all the goddesses. 80.
In all Buddha-fields without exception, he brings forth the emanations of the Buddhas;
he displays the Buddha-activities through the emanations of the Buddhas... ||81||
For he becomes [the master] of all states of being without exception within the three realms, through the dancing of the *ḍākinī* net of the union of all vajras. 82.
One should satisfy Śarva and the world through the various forms and ritual sequences of the Buddhas, Vajradhara, and others, by means of the miraculous displays of the lotus-net. 83.
He shall display all the activities of the great sovereignty over the three realms, accomplished through peace and war by means of the miraculous transformations of royal illusion. (84)
Having seized the great sovereignty of the three realms through his own heroic deeds, he should demonstrate the crushing of the entire world by means of the horse-dance. 85.

By means of these and other [pledges] without end, equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) and as limitless as the realm of space, [they are established] through the universal vows in every respect. 86.
The Tathāgata Śrīvajrasattva, who provides space for all space, sports with various glorious displays of the play of delight. (87)
By means of all that is universally auspicious, by means of all universal vows, and through universal discipline, he shall bring the realm of sentient beings to perfection. (88)
These and others, infinite in extent and equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), as limitless as the realm of space, are all the supreme ones, beginning with the Buddhas. (89)
Established in the glorious Vajrasattva within the expanse of all space, they enter into all [beings] for the sake of accomplishing the sovereignty of the siddhis. 90.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śrī Vajrasattva,
from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyogadākinījālasaṃvara*.
The sixth chapter: The Ritual of the Maṇḍala of the Net of Dakinis, the Union of All Buddhas.
Henceforth, I shall proclaim the miraculous manifestation of all the cakras—the supreme, universal, and all-pervading [nature] of the deities of Śrī Vajrasattva. (1)
One should accomplish [the practice] in a secret, supremely delightful place, within the Self of all, or likewise in a secluded spot, or again in one's own garden and such. ||2||
Being auspicious for the universe in every respect, and through all universal vows, one should accomplish all universal activities at ease in every way. (3)
In monasteries, forest hermitages, and on mountain peaks everywhere, one should accomplish the various and manifold activities of a Buddha. 4.
Established in a cremation ground, a temple of the gods, or the abodes of the Mothers and so forth, the various activities of the glorious Vajradhara are accomplished. (5)
In delightful lotus gardens and at the confluences of rivers, the activities of the glorious Padmadhara are accomplished in the ultimate sense. (6)
Indeed, in delightful royal capitals and in royal gardens,
he shall accomplish various and manifold tasks of state.
Indeed, on variegated mountain peaks and along the banks of rivers,
as well as in accomplished foreign kingdoms, one should train the vajra-horses.
In every way, with all types of attire and all means, one should accomplish the activities of Śrī Vajrasattva through the practice of the maṇḍala and so forth. 9.
The lotus of the Buddhas is red, while that of Vajrapāṇi is variegated;
that of Lokeśvara is white in color, and that of Śrīvajrabhāskara is yellow. 10.
"O one of all colors, just as external canopies, banners,
and ornaments constitute the complete decoration of the thunderbolt-wielding Śrī Paramāśva," thus [it was said].
Just as it is in its proper place, according to its wheel, according to its array, and according to the world—so does the Supreme Lord create such a wheel for the assembly. 12.
Whatever eternal merit there is from the direct vision of the mandala of the deities of Śrī Vajrasattva, such [merit] likewise arises from what is subsequently written. (13)
The wise one should trace out the mandala, which brings about equality in all directions, with four lines for the cardinal points and eight mandalas, extending east, west, and north. 14.
Who is capable of constructing mandalas according to their true nature?
The construction of mandalas is accomplished through union with one's own tutelary deity. 15.
Through the yoga of one's own self as the deity, all accomplishments are brought about;
even if the ritual procedure is deficient or excessive, it is perfected and does not incur fault. ||16||
It is auspicious for the universe in every respect, it belongs to the wielder of the universal wheel in every respect;
it is perfected as the universe in every respect, and it is the universal mandala in every respect. 17.
The mandala of the Buddha is circular; that of the Vajrin is like a half-moon;
that of the Excellent Lotus is in the form of a lotus; and that of the Excellent Jewel is in the form of a jewel.
These may be made according to one's desire, according to external circumstances, according to the time, and according to what is comfortable. (18)
The mandala of Vajrapāṇi is established as the glorious supreme horse;
for there is no samaya for one who is devoid of the mandala or who has abandoned it. 19.

Some ritual accomplishment may be achieved by one who does not know the secret of reality; however, one must never commit the killing of living beings, nor should one ever abandon the Three Jewels. 20.

One must certainly never abandon the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), nor the auspicious teacher; one must likewise never forsake various musical instruments, that which is most auspicious, the truth, the ten wholesome actions, song, and indeed everything else as well. 21.
O fortunate one, through the means of one's own self, the Blessed One is the bringer of universal fortune;
whereas those who hate the commitments are unfortunate, being joined with the doctrine of selflessness.
The Blessed Buddha is fortunate because he has completely purified existence;
the Śrāvakas are unfortunate in this world because they have attained ultimate parinirvāṇa. || 23 ||
The illustrious Vajrapāṇi is fortunate because he accomplishes all ritual manuals;
the Pratyekabuddhas are unfortunate because of their excessive application to emptiness;
Avalokiteśvara is fortunate because of the purification of all passion. (24)
In this world, the heretics are unfortunate, being possessed of false views;
whereas the glorious Vajrasūrya is fortunate, due to his accumulation of the supreme ultimate truth. 25.
All those ascetics are unfortunate, for they have renounced even their own bodies;
whereas he is fortunate due to his possession of the supreme horse, glory, and the entirety of the kingdom's preeminent wealth.
All those selfless mendicants who possess nothing are unfortunate. (26)
The master is indeed fortunate because he accomplishes his own self through all forms of bliss;
but all the disciples are unfortunate, for they have wrong views and are hostile toward the samaya.
By understanding this secret reality clearly in its true meaning, one achieves the state of all Buddhas, just as the word of all Buddhas declares. (28)

But one who is established as a master for all [practitioners] should clearly explain to the disciples and others the secret reality (guhyatattva) of infinite extent to those who seek the mandala from the east. 29.
At the times of entering the circle, one should ask, "Who are you, O dear one?
And upon entering, the beloved should say, "I am fortunate. ||30||
One should cause the secret nature to enter into the secret reality;
likewise, one who has entered the maṇḍala and offered the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). ||31||
One who knows the ritual of the secret reality attains the supreme imperishable;
for the Teacher of the Universe, he offers the highest sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) which is success in every respect.
That which is to be renounced by someone is considered his supreme [offering]. ||32||
Whatever is most beloved or even more distinguished, that indeed should be given to the guru by one who desires that very thing to be imperishable. ||33||
If his desired object be wealth, or even some task to be performed, that should be given or that task done; for even one's own gain is indeed excellent.
If this [gift] should be the best, he must also give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā);
by insulting his preceptor in every way, he incurs eternal suffering.
Having adorned a maiden and likewise his beloved wife,
he should give them away and then redeem them by paying their price as the supreme offering for the enlightenment of a Buddha;
and having offered a great animal, he should again redeem it by its price.
The union with Śrīvajradhara... [bestows] the dakṣiṇā;
likewise, a pure string of pearls, a very white garment, a white horse, and for the lotus-bearer, the boon-granting dakṣiṇā. ||37||
Various objects of royal enjoyment, collections of garments and ornaments, and likewise all forms of worship constitute the offering for Vajrasūrya. (38)
Having made a horse well-adorned, or an elephant well-equipped,
or a chariot filled with jewels, one should give it as the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) for the King of Horses.

Alternatively, the wise one should fashion it in various ways with substances consisting of all elements, as well as with precious gems, and by means of the consecrations of the jewel-like Buddhas. 40.
On his crown, forehead, both sides, and likewise on his back, he wears the great jewel-diadem of all the Buddhas; he is the supreme syllable.
Or likewise, [the deities] may consist of all the elements, or consist of the life-force and the roots;
they likewise possess a crown-jewel of skulls and a Buddha as their crest-gem. 42.

For one who always offers [this] to the Universal Guru, the Teacher of All, success is achieved through the perfect accomplishment of the entire kingdom, in its totality and without exception. || 43 ||
An image made of a single jewel, or likewise of various jewels, [is consecrated] by the Buddha-lotus empowerments and by the empowerment of all the disciples. 44.
For the Buddhas, there is the Jewel-Vajra; likewise, the Vajra in the Vajra family.
For Avalokiteśvara, who is the Buddha-body, there is likewise the Jewel-Bearer, Maṇi. ||45||
The Jewel of the Buddha, likewise the Lotus, the Vajra, and the Wish-fulfilling Gem;
this is the compendium of self-consecration for all the supreme and ultimate [deities]. (46)
Whether they are cast, forged, refined, or painted, one should fashion various and highly diverse seals and marks. 47.
The self-arisen signs and mudrās are auspicious in every way;
they are all goddesses of great bliss, extending to the limits of the realm of space. 48.
Likewise, Dhanurbāṇa, Subhaga, and Subhaga;
and Kapāla, Khaṭvāṅga, and Viśvavajra as well. ||49||
In the Viśvapadma [mandala], Amitāyus is the accomplisher of the lifespan of all Buddhas; the entire host of goddesses is perfected, as is the supreme collection of symbols and mudrās. 50.
The Bāṇa and Brahmaśiras [missiles], as well as the Cakra-mudrā;
the Vajra, the foremost Triśūla-mudrā, and likewise the Kalpavṛkṣa and its creeper. ||51||
Likewise, Padma, Heyocchraya-grīva, Haritāśvamukha, Varāhadaṃṣṭrā, Siddhā, as well as Candra and Sūrya. ||52||
One who knows the ritual of the secret reality attains the supreme imperishable;
for the Teacher of the Universe, the highest sacrificial fee is success itself.
That which is to be renounced by someone is considered the most excellent offering for that person. (32)
Whatever is most beloved, or even whatever is most excellent—that indeed should be given to the teacher by one who desires that very thing to be inexhaustible. (33)
If he should desire either wealth or even some service, that should be given or performed; for even one's own gain is indeed excellent. (34)
If this [gift] should be the best, he must also give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā);
by insulting his preceptor in every way, he incurs eternal suffering. ||35||
Having adorned a maiden and likewise his beloved wife,
he should give them away and then redeem them by paying their price as the supreme offering for the enlightenment of a Buddha;
and having offered a great animal, he should again redeem it by its price.
The union with Śrīvajradhara... [is] the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
A pure string of pearls, a very white garment, a white horse, and a lotus-bearer as the excellent sacrificial fee. 37.
Various objects of royal enjoyment, collections of garments and ornaments, as well as every form of worship, constitute the offering to Vajrasūrya. (38)
Having adorned a horse well, or a well-equipped elephant,
or a chariot filled with jewels, one should give it as the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) for the King of Horses.
Alternatively, the wise one should fashion it in various ways using all kinds of precious substances or with gems of living value, through the consecrations of the Buddha-jewels. 40.
Upon his crown, forehead, both sides, and likewise his back, he wears the great jewel-crown of all Buddhas; he is the supreme syllable.
Or likewise with those made of all the elements, or even those consisting of the life-force and roots;
likewise with a crown-jewel of skulls and a crest-gem of the Buddha. ||42||
To the universal teacher, the teacher of all, at all times;
through the perfect accomplishment of the entire kingdom, without exception or remainder, [everything] is accomplished in every respect. ||43||
An image made of a single jewel, as well as one of variegated jewels, is consecrated by the Buddha-lotus consecrations and by the consecration of all the disciples. (44)
For the Buddhas, there is the Jewel-Vajra; likewise, the Vajra in the Vajra family.
For Avalokiteśvara, who is the Buddha-body, there is the Jewel-holder, the Maṇi. ||45||
The Jewel of the Buddha, likewise the Lotus, the Vajra, and the Wish-fulfilling Gem;
this is the compendium of self-consecration for all the supreme and most excellent [deities]. (46)
Whether they are cast, forged, refined, or painted—whether variegated or exquisitely adorned—one should fashion them with the appropriate marks and seals. 47.
The self-arisen signs and mudrās are auspicious in every way;
they are all goddesses of great bliss, extending as far as the realm of space. 48.
Likewise, Dhanurbāṇa, Subhaga, and Subhagas;
also Kapāla, Khaṭvāṅga, and Viśvavajra. ||49||
In the Viśvapadma [mandala], Amitāyus is the accomplisher of the lifespan of all Buddhas; the assembly of all goddesses is perfected, as is the supreme assembly of symbols and mudrās. 50.
The Bāṇa and Brahmaśiras [missiles], as well as the Cakra mudrā, the Vajra, the foremost Triśūla mudrā, and likewise the Kalpavṛkṣa and its creepers. ||51||
Likewise, Padma, Heyocchraya, Grīva, Haritāśvamukha, Varāhadaṃṣṭrā, Siddhā, as well as Candra and Sūrya. 52.
Within the great vessel of the universal lotus is the elixir of the Buddha-form, auspicious with the taste of the essence of all beings; it is the supreme multitude of signs and mudrās. 53.
The flute, the sarvavīṇā lute, the mukunda drum, and likewise the muraja drum;
the flower, the incense, the lamp, and likewise the garment of the universe (viśvavāsa). ||54||
These and other such excellent multitudes of signs and mudrās are infinite in extent, equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), and as limitless as the realm of space (ākāśadhātu). ||55||
In the entire expanse of space, they are established as the glorious Vajrasattva;
through the attainments of sovereignty and the accomplishment of the self of all, they abide in meditative absorption. (56)
The robe, the bowl, and likewise the mendicant’s staff, as well as the book of the True Dharma, and the collection of other insignia and seals. ||57||
The tongue, the seal (mudrā), as well as the bell and the musical instrument, the vajra, and the jewel-casket—this is the supreme group of symbolic seals (cihnamudrā). ||58||
Likewise, the image of the Buddha, the mirror, the offering of wind, the thunderbolt, the lightning, the cloud, and similarly the eye-seal (netramudrā). ||59||
A flame, a vajra, a khaṭvāṅga, a skull-cup, and likewise a chalice;
great blood, great fat, great flesh, and great honey. 60.
A sharp arrow, as well as a magnet, liquor, water, and likewise a creeper tossed by the wind, and even a cloth and fire; || 61 ||
The illustrious Vajrakrodharāja indeed [is the master] for devouring all wicked beings and the like;
the host of his symbolic mudrās is perfected, accomplishing the attainments of yoga. (62)
The seven lotuses at the tips of the insignia are the universal lotus, and those colored red, green, white, blue, yellow, and madder-red. 63.
The lotus, the needle, the Nārīmudrā, and likewise the wheel of Dharma;
the trident that brings prosperity, the vajra, and the supreme group of lotus symbols. 64.
The bow, the arrow, and the sword, as well as the flame of splendor; likewise, the consecration during the rite of consecration, or worship, which is a collection of emblems. ||65||
Likewise, the universal lotus and the universal vajra—these two symbolic mudrās are perfected as the subduer of all kingdoms. (66)
All things, both stable and moving, from all the Buddhas onwards without exception, as far as the limits of the realm of space, are the signs and seals of the Self-Existent One. 67.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śrī Vajrasattva,
from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyogadākinījālasaṃvara*.
The seventh [chapter], the ritual manual for the knowledge of the mudrās of all maṇḍalas.
Hereafter, I shall explain the miraculous manifestation of all worship, the supreme universal array of the goddesses of Śrī Vajrasattva. (1)

With his left and right hands dancing from the tips to the base of his body, the glorious one has his left cheek resting [on his hand]; with his right hand in the *tripatāka* gesture, he is full of grace and charm, preceded by a gentle smile, and is the very eye of the world. (2)
One should mentally prostrate to Śrī Vajrasattva with trembling devotion;

one should instantly offer oneself to the Holder of the Vajra of the Perfect Buddhas, Padma-Vajra-Sūrya, and the Three Realms—what need is there for such an offering among those whose pride has been uprooted? (3)
Having quickly bowed down with humility before Rudra, Indra, Upendra, along with Candra, Arka, Yama, and Īśa, one should employ [the mantra] in all ritual actions. 4.
Having performed worship to the Buddha with prostrations made by a trembling heart, he joined his palms in the form of a vajra, encircled by the glory of all accomplishments without exception. (5)
By means of drawing up his left eyebrow and through his laughter and speech,
he could destroy the three worlds, including Brahmā, Upendra, and Rudra.

Having placed a lotus from the bud-like añjali gesture at the heart, one should bow to those who have entered one's own yoga by means of the four petals formed by the two thumbs and the two little fingers, which are fully blossomed and slightly inclined.
Bowing with all his limbs upon the earth, well-established in his posture, he should incline himself in salutation with joined palms to the heart, the mouth, and likewise the head. 8.
The glorious one, maintaining vajra-pride, smiling with his eyes, should bow down; he would cause the three worlds to prostrate—what need is there to mention those who are arrogant in their power? 9.
Thus ends the knowledge of the seal of the means of valid cognition.
Whatever hand-gestures and dramatic expressions are found in the treatises on dance, those mudrās of Śrī Vajrasattva accomplish the attainment of one's own purpose. (10)
With all graceful movements brought forth by every mode of possession, one should offer all worship through dances that encompass the entire universe. ||11||
With the left and right hands dancing from the tips of the body to its end, the left hand forms the *khaṭaka* at the front, while the right hand is in the *tripatāka* gesture. 12.
By sealing with this mudrā, the assembly of all Buddhas is accomplished through the supreme great siddhis and the sovereign powers of Maheśvara. 13.
The assembly of all Buddhas is the mudrā named Śrīsubhagā.
Having lifted it up by means of yoga, let the great planet carry it away;
having turned it over, he should place all [the contents] within his skull upon his head. 14.
Then, having brought [the deity] down into the state of dancing through all-enveloping dances, one who is graced by the song of the syllable *HŪṂ* should present every offering. ||15||
The mudrā named Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-subhaga-śrīmahāsukha.
With the left and right hands, dancing from the tips of the body to its base, one should form the vajrāñjali mudrā and likewise turn to the left. ||16||
Having raised them up through yoga, one should place them at the junction of the head;
being graced by the song of the syllable Om, one should offer all worship. ||17||
The mudrā named "Worship of the Buddhas" consists of the hands joined in the *vajrāñjali* gesture, adorned with the *śrīvajravali*.
With the left and right hands, dancing from the body to the fingertips, one performs the rite of all offerings and oblations with the upward-spread vajra-añjali mudrā. ||18||
With this mudrā, by means of the dances performed during the entry into the cremation ground,
one who is graced by the vajra-limbed laughter should present all offerings.
The ritual for all offerings and bali-oblations: the Śrī Heruka-vajra-cupped-palms gesture. ||19||
With the left and right hands dancing from the extremities of the body to its core, one should offer all worship with rhythmic claps performed clockwise and counter-clockwise. ||20||
The name-seal of Śrī Padmanāla Narteśvarī.
With the left and right hands, dancing from the tips of the body to the extremities, one should form the *cakraratna-añjali* mudrā and present all offerings. ||21||
The seal named Śrīvajraratna, which fulfills all aspirations.
They cast upwards, they cast downwards, they whirl about, and likewise they smear;
they set in motion the offerings of flowers, incense, lamps, and foremost perfumes. ||22||
Whether complete or empty, or again according to what is available, all offerings are equally successful when accompanied by the commitments and practices. 23.
By means of these supreme mudrās, all the Buddhas have been worshipped;
they in turn worship all [practitioners] with the accomplishments, sovereign powers, and attainments for the sake of success. ||24||
Among them, some noble and excellent women, equal to the dharmadhātu and as vast as the realm of space, performed all manner of worship for the Self-Existent Ones. (25)
That which has not been performed by him, nor even accumulated—[is] the Great Bliss of the Sovereignty of Yoga through the Union with all Buddhas. 26.

Indeed, for them, there is nothing whatsoever that is unattainable; likewise, the blissful activity of accomplishment is perfectly achieved, without exception or remainder, through the spreading accomplishments of the mudrās.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śrīvajrasattva, from the *Sarvabuddhasamāyogadākinījālasaṃvara*. 28.
The eighth [chapter], the Ritual Manual of the Samaya, titled "The Auspicious Glory of the Union of All Offerings."
Hereafter, I shall proclaim the miraculous manifestation of all the Buddhas, the supreme universal sovereignty of the deities of Śrī Vajrasattva. (1)
Abiding eternally within the supreme, delightful secret, which is the self of all, the being consisting of all Buddhas is Vajrasattva, the ultimate bliss. 2.
Because he is the dawn of all bliss and because of the purity of all bliss, Vajrasattva, whose body is as radiant as the full moon, is supreme happiness. (3)
The Blessed One is indeed Great Passion, because he has internalized all passion;
he is this seal of Śrī Vajrasattva, with a red heart and blazing radiance. (4)
There is no other jewel in the three realms equal to the Jewel of the Buddha;
indeed, he is supreme because of this crown of the great jewel of all Buddhas. (5)
Furthermore, it is unassailable, pure with divine water, and is indeed perfected by its very nature through its own power and inherent character. (6)
Wearing a crown of garlands of skulls and having the Buddha as his crest-jewel, he becomes the lord of afflicted world-systems, such as Sahā and others; thus he attains accomplishment. (7)
Through the union with Śrī Vajrasattva and the assemblies of all goddesses, he who is auspiciously endowed with the universal totality attains success through every *aralli*. ||8||
Having deluded and then raised up the Sambuddha, Vajradhṛk, Padma, Cakra, and Sūrya, along with the three realms, one should employ them in all ritual actions by means of the mudrā. 9.
By sealing with this mudrā and commanding, "Fall! for one who desires to fly up, the glorious Vajrasattva, the bestower of boons upon all goddesses, becomes accomplished. 10.
The supreme union, the fortunate one, the seal named the playful sport of the commitment of Śrī Vajrasattva.
By means of the union of the left and right [channels], through the engagement in blissful absorption, and having assumed the sattva-paryaṅka posture, one shatters all the armies. ||11||
This is the mudrā named Śrīvajrasattvarājaparyaṅka.
Their faces possess smiles with the hue of the moon due to the purity of all things;
yet, through the purity of ruby-red [light], their thighs and waists are reddish-fair. 12.

Those with arms as dark as the tips of palāśa leaves possess happiness and sovereignty; likewise, due to their pleasant touch and sovereignty, those with a union of white and yellow [complexion] possess great wealth. ||13||
Wherever the function of the rule for the phonemes was applied, there appeared goddesses who were the great phonemes of the universe, their radiance agitated by universal flames. (14)
They are established upon universal lotuses, grounded in total purity;
they wear various ornaments and garments made of excellent jewels, such as the lotus of the Buddha. ||15||
Together with those adorned by the assembly of all Buddhas, [they act] through means that especially involve attracting, warding off, and seizing. (16)
The "Seizer of All Limbs" is perfected by the mudrā of one's own embrace;
with this mudrā, one who desires it causes [the target] to fall or fly up.
The glorious Vajrasattva, the lord of all desires, becomes accomplished. ||17||
The mudrā named Śrīvajrasamvarakelīkilā, who is fortunate through the supreme passion of the atiyoga.
Through the arousal of bliss through attachment to various samayas,
the supreme deity is the best mudrā who embraces one's own self.
By means of this mudrā, the yogi who desires to fly is cast down;
thus the glorious Vajrasattva, the Lord of Great Bliss, is accomplished. 18.
The name-seal of the playful sport of the samaya-vow of Śrī Vajrasattva, who is fortunate through the supreme bliss of atiyoga.
By means of the yoga of the sacred thread (yajñopavīta), there is the grasping of the vajra and khaṭvāṅga;
together with the mudrā of self-embrace at the tips of the lotus and the double-vajra (viśvavajra). 19.
By means of this mudrā, one falls, flies up, or remains stationary;
thus the King, Vajrasattva, the Lord of all Yogins, is accomplished. (20)
The name-seal of the playful sport of the vow of yoga with Śrī Vajrasattva, who is fortunate through the supreme bliss of the Atiyoga.
The cup of all Buddhas and Siddhas, with the mudrā of the beautiful embrace, is the supreme deity in the midst of the union of Śrī Vajrasattva and his consort. 21.
Having sealed [himself] with this mudrā, the yogi, desiring to fly up, falls;
he attains the state of Vajrasattva, endowed with adamantine life, youth, and glory. ||22||
The illustrious Vajrāyus, fortunate through the supreme passion of the Atiyoga, is the name-seal (*nāmamudrā*) of those who sport in the *saṃvara*.
These and others are infinite in extent, equal to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), as limitless as the expanse of space; they are the self-arisen seals of the universe (*viśvamudrā*). (23)
In the expanse of all space, they are established as the glorious Vajrasattva;
they enter [into union] through the accomplishments, sovereignties, and renowned attainments of the self of all. (24) Thus it is said.
The host of root mudrās of the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-ḍākinījālasamvara*.
Just as, by means of the essence of the end of the scriptures, through the four throws of the arrow performed at the sacred site of Śrīpūrṇā, there was the defeat of the four Māras. || 25 ||
The head of Mahābrahmā is the mudrā named Śrīvajrasāyaka.
By the movements of placing, shifting, contracting, and extending the feet, and by the upward lifting of the wheel-mudrā, the leaping across the three worlds is accomplished. ||26||
