The name-seal of Śrī Vajranārāyaṇī.
By means of the specific mudrās of drawing in (karaṇa), warding off (vāraṇa), and especially of seizing (haraṇa), he should cause the three worlds to dance and then withdraw them. 27.
The mudrā named Śrīvajratālanartteśvarī.
By taking hold of whichever creeper belongs to any woman and embracing her with his own embrace, he delights all women; thus, he becomes a manifest wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣa). ||28||
The mudrā named Śrīvajrakāmadevī.
Together with Rudra, Upendra, and Indra, as well as Candra, Arka, Yama, and Īśa, he could even dry up the three worlds with his gusts of wind from tasting [the nectar]. ||29||
This is the mudrā of the venerable Vajrapadmavaḍa (or Vaśva) Vāmukha.
Together with Rudra, Indra, Upendra, along with Candra, Arka, and Yama, he should withdraw the three worlds by means of the tasting of the nose and the sound of *sītkāra*. 30.
The name-seal of Śrī Vajravārāhī.
Together with Rudra, Indra, Upendra, along with Candra, Ārka, Yama, and Īśa—one may even consume the three worlds by means of the gaze of tasting. 31.
This is the name-seal (nāmamudrā) of Śrī Vajrasūrya, Candra, and Hutāsana.
By means of the tasting of the Self of all, one could even restore to life the ashes, together with Rudra, Indra, Upendra, along with Candra, Ārka, and Yama. 32.
The mudrā named Śrīvajradhātu-punaḥsaṃjīvanī.

By means of the application of the bamboo-gesture (*vaṃśābhinaya*) and by acting according to the respective modes of possession (*āveśa*), one may bring the three worlds—including Brahmā, Upendra, and Rudra—under one's control. ||33||
The name-seal of Śrīvajravaṃśavaśaṃkarī.

Through the application of the lute gesture and by engaging in the movements according to the [divine] possession, one achieves all accomplishments through the swift success of the expansion of ritual actions. ||34||
The mudrā named Śrīvajravīṇāsukhapramohanī.

By means of the expressive gestures of Mukunda and by acting out according to his various states of possession, the yogi can instantly dispel fevers, demonic seizures, poisons, attachments, and all sufferings. ||35||
The illustrious Vajramukundā is the name-seal (nāmamudrā) that removes all suffering.
Through the gestures of the drum and by acting out according to his inspiration, the yogi can, in an instant, cause the entire three worlds to enter into a state of possession. ||36||
The mudrā named Śrīvajramṛdaṅgonmādanī.
Through the offering of mudrās and dance, the self-arisen ones accomplish the worship of all things—without exception or remainder—by means of the continuous performance of dance-worship. (37)
Indeed, fevers, poisons, artificial toxins, diseases, the afflictions of ḍākinīs, and planetary seizures are pacified in an instant by the dances of the Viśvamaṇḍalikās. 38.
Sealed by Rudra, Indra, Upendra, along with Candra, Arka, and Yama, it indeed revives in an instant those who have been devoured while deluded. 39.
These and others are infinite in number, equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), as vast as the realm of space; they are the self-arisen goddesses and mudrās. 40.
In the expanse of all space, they are established as Śrī Vajrasattva;
they enter [all beings] through the accomplishments, sovereignties, and renown of the self, by means of the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasamvara*. (41)
Through songs that are perfectly accomplished, unsurpassed siddhi has been attained.
Now, this song of Śrī Vajrasattva, which accomplishes all activities and brings about the ultimate transcendence of existence, [is taught] for the sake of this knowledge of mudrās. 42.

O Śrīmukha Vajrasattva, fortunate one, I take refuge in you! O Buddha, O you of manifold and diverse lineage, for the welfare of the world, grant me the supreme accomplishment! O you who are the blissful self of all Tathāgatas, the variegated samvara of the ḍākinī-net! Ala la la la la hoḥ!

Display the wondrous drama of the Tathāgata-yoga! JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ SAMAYA HO SUKHODDHARA VIKURVA HŪṂ DĪPETA! A LA LA LA LA HOḤ! Enter the disciple! By this, the entire net of the diverse Ḍākinīs of all the Tathāgatas is perfectly accomplished everywhere, in every way, and as everything.
The knowledge of the mudrās of the maṇḍala of the yoga of the ḍākinīs of the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga*.
He alone is the Blessed One, the yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata;
for the sake of the purification of all liberation, he is established in the seal of the glorious Buddha. (43)
Because he is pure in the ultimate sense, he bears the color of molten gold;
because he is the great passion that transcends dispassion and so forth, his radiant luster is variegated with white. 44.
Apart from the jewel of the Dharma, there is nothing that accomplishes the status of a King of Dharma.
The Bodhicitta of the Mahāyāna is the Victor brought forth by the Vajra-jewel; [it is formed] by the right thumb and forefinger upon the left hand in the *khaṭaka* gesture. 45.
By touching all the fingers together, it is established as the Root Mudrā.
This is the manifest Perfection of Wisdom of all Buddhas, which brings about the great arousal of the thought of enlightenment and the turning of the Wheel of Dharma. (46)
Seal this method of the Perfection of Wisdom with this mudrā;
thus it proceeds, extending as far as the limits of the realm of space. 47.

The arouser of the great awakening mind and the turner of the wheel of Dharma—the Buddha alone is indeed to be realized; the Buddha is supremely eternal. Those who behold him as united [with reality] worship him in every way.
The Buddhas, who are supremely eternal, were seen and indeed worshipped by them. ||48||
This is the seal named Śrīsamaya, which simultaneously brings about the arising of the thought [of awakening] and the turning of the wheel of the sublime Dharma.
Trampling upon his right limb and conquering all his left limbs,
he sits in the sattvaparyaṅka posture and shatters all the Māras.
The glorious sattvaparyaṅka posture.
Having formed the vajra-fist and covered [the head] with the left hand, one achieves success through the accomplishments of the complete and exhaustive *saṃgīti* of all the Buddhas. ||50||
Likewise, when covered by the Great Vajra Fist of Śrī Heruka, one attains accomplishment through the complete and total attainments of the songs of the heroes. ||51||

The fist consisting of the lotus and the woman, likewise concealed by the left [hand], is perfected through the accomplishments of the entire course of conduct for enlightenment, both in its totality and in its particulars. ||52||
The fist that grasps the jewel, concealed by the left hand, is accomplished through the attainments of all the purposes of every Buddha, without exception or remainder. ||53||
Having formed the Buddha-fist and covered it with the left hand, one attains success through all the excellent accomplishments of every single Buddha, without exception. ||54||
Having assumed the *nārīmudrā* and covered [the organ] with the left hand, one attains success through all the *siddhis*, including the *asusiddhis*, without exception or remainder. ||55||
The Śrīparamāśvamuṣṭi mudrā, concealed by the left hand, accomplishes all rites—without exception—in their entirety through the attainment of all success. ||56||
The fist of the illustrious Siddhalocanā, concealed by the left hand, accomplishes all worldly successes without exception through the attainments of the entire world. 57.
The first is the *Buddhasaṃgīti*, the second is the *Śauriṇī*, the third is the *Samantabhadrā*, and the fourth is the *Akṣayakaraṇḍakā*. (58)
The Blessed One, the Goddess of All Buddhas, the Dhāraṇī of the Auspicious Face, likewise.
The seventh is Mahāmeghā, and the eighth is Gaganalocanā. ||59||
The seal of all dhāraṇīs.
And through this knowledge of mudrās, which accomplishes all supreme rites, the supreme syllable—the emanation of the Buddhas sung in harmony—is perfected. 60.
One should sing the *utthāpanī*, *dhruvā*, *siddhā*, *viśvā*, and likewise the *sāritaka* according to the six-limbed scale (*ṣaḍaṅga-grāma*), which brings about the state of *dhaivata*. 61.
The vast expanse of the realms is filled with many worlds numbering as many as atoms;
it is filled with the attainments of all the goals of the Victors, numbering as many as atoms. (62)
Manifest with multitudes of emanated bodies numbering as many atoms, manifest with the Tathāgatas’ excellent transformations numbering as many atoms—hoḥ! 63.

O Śrī Vairocana-yoga, who manifests the various miraculous transformations of all the Tathāgatas through the great bliss of ultimate existence—A LA LA LA LA HOḤ! May you grant me success this very day! 64.
For when this is sung, it is accomplished; there is no doubt about this.
It is the *Ḍākinījālasamvara*, the union with all space. 65.
Then, having performed worship with flowers and other offerings according to the detailed ritual procedure by means of the four women through the secret reality of oneself; ||66||
The Knowledge of the Seal of the Tathāgata.
That very Blessed One is Yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata;
for the sake of purifying poisons, he clearly manifests the glorious mudrā of the cremation ground.
Toward those who are extremely wicked and fierce, gentleness is appropriate;
such is the yoga consisting of wisdom and skillful means, the supreme vow of yoga. 68.
The supreme dissolution into the ashes of the wrathful deities arising from the Buddha's mind consists of a being composed of blue flames, with a mandala shining with red flames. ||69||
And it was not subject to seizure by others, being pure with divine water;
for it was perfected by its very nature, through its own power and inherent character.
The Great Garment, the Great Consecration, the Great Meat, and the Great Honey—she who has become one with all the cremation grounds is the glorious Seal of the Supreme Lord. 71.
For the sake of purifying the realm of sentient beings who are exceedingly wicked, fierce, and foremost, this is the supreme seal of the Great Vajra Śrī Heruka. 72.
Wearing a crown of garlands of skulls and likewise having the Buddha as his crest-jewel,
he attains success through the complete and total accomplishment of all royal powers,
accompanied by the resonant ringing sounds of the vajra, khaṭvāṅga, and vajra-bell. (73)
Through the miraculous manifestations of the universal mudrā of the absorption of Śrī Heruka,
having sealed and deluded the Fully Awakened One Vajradhṛk, Padma, and Vajrasūrya— the threefold realm— he shall restore even that [victim] to life as ashes. 74.
The name-seal of Padmanarteśvarī, the manifestation of the great vajra-entrance that is the cause of glory.
By means of the sacred thread (yajñopavīta), the skull-topped staff (khaṭvāṅga) rests upon his two sides;
in his left hand he holds a skull-cup, while in his right is the triple-bannered gesture (tripatākā).
By means of the space-mudrā, the yogi becomes the supreme lord of all space;
from space, he brings forth women and other excellent jewels, as well as all phenomena. ||76||
By means of this mudrā, through the gestures of striking down those to be subdued, that sky-farer brings them all down in happiness and enjoys them as his own objects of enjoyment. 77.
Having struck down with his illusory powers this inexhaustible host of Rudra, Upendra, Candra, Ārka, and the Ḍākinīs, that sky-goer devours them all without remainder. (78)
The name-seal of the *Sarvākāśasamatāsamāyogasubhagaśrīvajraḍākinīsamvara*.

By means of the application of the left and right [hands], proceeding with easy immersion, and assuming the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka), one should perform the sequence of the Varuṇa-cakra. ||79||
Having sealed, utterly deluded, raised up, and made to dance [the victim] along with Rudra, Indra, Upendra, Candra, Ārka, Yama, and Aṃśa, one should consume it. ||80||
But by this very yoga, having pressed with the squeezing of the thighs and mouth, and having ground it into powder and scattered it, one should drink it. 81.
By these very illusions, through the vibrations within her thighs, that fortunate woman shall subdue all noble men, both divine and human. 82.
The mudrā named Śrīvajraraudrāsamā, auspicious through its union with the touch of all happiness.
Henceforth, I shall explain the established universal mudrās within the maṇḍala of the Buddha-Ḍākinīs, who are the absorption of Śrī Heruka. 83.
Gentle, fierce, deluded, seizing, joyful, dancing, and full of grace;
dead, as if dead, and risen from the dead—these are established as the mudrās of bliss.
The forms [of the deities] arise from the peaceful, fierce, and deluded states, and consist of dancing and postures. (84)
The mudrās of vision are supremely accomplished through the secret yogic vows;
likewise, there are the foremost applications of flowers and incense, as well as wine, water, and creepers. (85)
For those who have attained perfection through the offering of cloth and fire especially seal themselves;
yet the marks of yoga, despite their one-pointed application, do not bestow happiness. 86.

Taking up a spray of water, she sprinkled him; with the expulsion of her breath, she performed the *nāsana* (nose-touching); with her left eye, she drew him toward her hand, as well as performing kissing and embracing. (87)
Dancing, the delusion of pleasure, eating, and the secret form;
likewise, the head of Mahābrahmā and the leaping across the three worlds. ||88||
The lifting of the earth, likewise the gesture of one's own mudrā, dancing in the cremation ground, and likewise the whirlwind; ||89||
The great dissolution and the fire [of destruction] are established as the *karmamudrās*.
The first is the sealing *mudrā*, the second is the heart-piercing, the third is the deluding, and likewise the fourth is the raising-up. 90.
The fifth is the dancing mudrā, and the sixth is the slaying mudrā;
the seventh is the devouring mudrā, and likewise the eighth is the action mudrā.
Now, [I shall describe] the unsurpassed counter-mudrā for all these mudrās. 91.
I shall explain in detail that which distinguishes the nature of all mudrās, while remaining established in the glorious Vajrapadma and performing vajra-songs, recitations, and dances. (92)
Whatever is consumed while sealed with the mudrā, even ashes, he shall bring back to life.
Now, I shall specifically proclaim the *Śrīvajrayogasaṃgīta*, which accomplishes all ritual actions for this knowledge of the mudrā. (93)
Having delighted her with various and manifold glances full of amorous play, and having gladdened her with diverse and varied kisses and embraces. (94)
Having partaken of all the various and manifold enjoyments of pleasure, display the great festival of the diverse and manifold samvara! 95.

Seal me! Delude me! Devour me! Restraining me, enter into great bliss! HŪṂ DĪEYI! Alala lala HOḤ! Manifest, manifest through the nets of the yoga-pledge (yoga-samvara)! PA I SA DU SA A LU SA MA HA SARVĀ Ā SU JO U!
Bhakṣaduṣālu santā āsajo u || 96 ||
By chanting this, one attains the *Sarvavajrasamāyogaḍākinījālasamvara*; there is no doubt about this. (97) Thus it is said.
This is the knowledge of the Śrī Heruka-vajra-mudrā.
That very Blessed One is Yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata;
for the sake of purifying all passion, he is established as the glorious Padma-mudrā.
Because he has attained the perfection of the supreme syllable, he resembles pure crystal. (98)
In order to dispel all passion, he possesses a radiance filled with various flames;
he is the Buddha adorned with diverse ornaments and garments set with jewels.
All the Buddhas, gathered together in assembly, are like the supreme realm of Sukhāvatī. (99)
Having turned back his hundred arms, which were dancing with various gestures and movements, he formed them into a circle marked by lotuses and lotus-signs. ||100||
Having thoroughly purified the triple world, especially by means of the lotus-nets of the Perfect Buddha Vajrasūrya, one should establish the Buddha in enlightenment. 101.
The mudrā named Śrī Padmanarteśvarī, auspicious through her diverse methods of discipline.
Seated in the half-lotus posture by means of the union of the left and right [channels], and having ascended the royal throne, one dispels all obstacles. ||102||
The mudrā named Śrīvajrapadmāsana.
Taking a red lotus with her left hand as she pleases, she causes the petals of the lotus to bloom through the yoga of exalting [the deity] within her own heart. 103.
Taking a palāśa lotus with the left hand as a face through the yoga of self-exaltation, one should bear the female consort (nārīmudrā) within one's own heart. 104.
Taking a white lotus with the left hand as is convenient, and forming the vajra-mudrā, one should turn the wheel of Dharma. 105.
Taking a blue lotus with the left hand as one pleases, one should dance with the right hand while the left is held in the *tripatāka* gesture. 106.
Taking a yellow lotus with the left hand as is comfortable, one should dance with the right hand raised in the *makāra* gesture. 107.
Taking with the left hand an excellent madder-red lotus out of pride, one should bear the vajra-mudrā through the application of self-exaltation in one's heart. (108)
Through Vilokinī one attains supreme enlightenment; through Viśuddhaśrī, a consort;

through Bhūriṇī, the status of a universal monarch (cakravartin); through Bhṛkuṭī, the seal of counter-sealing; and through Mahāśrīpadmavāsinī, sovereignty over the desires of the three worlds. Thus [it is said]. (109)
The vidyā-deities of the glorious Padmarāga.
Now, I shall specifically proclaim this Śrī Padmarāga-saṅgīta, which accomplishes all rites for this knowledge of mudrās. 110.
She assumes various forms such as those of all the Tathāgatas and others, and is supreme in the highest accomplishment for taming diverse and manifold sentient beings. 111.
O Pure Being, display your passion for the supreme lotus-array!
O Lord of the Dancing One, [exclaim] "A-la-la-la-la-hoḥ! and display your passion for liberation! 112.
I am the Buddha, I am the Holder of the Vajra, and I am Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara;
I am the Moon and the Sun—ala la la la la hoḥ! Padmajālaśrī! 113.
O you who perform many kinds of service, O pure one, O you who are free from pride! Ho! Ho! Ho!

O you who are the embodiment of the Buddha’s essence! O you who destroy the king of disputes, O you who bring about the complete destruction of delusion! O you who strike down those who strike down! O you who are the supreme moon of the great mountain!
By chanting this, one achieves success; there is no doubt about this:
the *Viśvapadmasamāyogadākinījālasaṃvara*. 114.
The Knowledge of the Mudrā of Śrī Padmanarteśvara.
That very Blessed One is Yoga, Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata;
for the sake of ultimate purity, the glorious Sun-seal is established. 115
Ākāśagarbha fulfills all hopes; through the non-confinement of space and so forth, he rains down all jewels, the most excellent of fine gems. 116.
In those who are exceedingly wicked and fierce, gentleness is not appropriate;
in the ultimate sense, the sun consists of wisdom and skillful means, and its very nature is brilliance. (117)
The world is subdued by majesty; it is accomplished through majesty alone.
It is desired that his deportment possesses the great splendor of the form of the sun. 118.
Intent on drawing the tip of his diamond bow and arrow, with his eyes rolling in amorous play... ||119||
By his majesty alone, he shall conquer the three worlds in their entirety, including Rudra, Indra, Upendra, along with Candra, Ārka, and Yama. 120.
The mudrā named Śrītrilokavijaya.
Having occupied his own seat with the two knees in the vajra-bind posture and having assumed the vajra-paryaṅka cross-legged position, he shall destroy all obstacles. ||121||
Śrīvajraparyaṅkā.
The Empowerment, the Deposition, the Great Ritual of the Banner-limb, and the Casting according to the specific inclination—these accomplish the attainment of one's own purpose. 122.
Now, I shall specifically proclaim the great song of Rājamāyā, which accomplishes all rites for this knowledge of mudrās. 123.
She who possesses all the various and supreme activities of sovereignty over the three worlds;
she who has won many diverse battles through her particular mode of warfare. 124.

O King Vajrasūrya, reveal yourself as the Samvara-net, which possesses the causes for various and manifold delusions and supreme deformities; [reveal] the clouds of the Bodhisattvas, which rain down the entire world of the equipment of generosity. 125
May he fulfill all hopes: *ala la la la la hoḥ*, reveal [it] quickly!
*ati se uṇi hāṇu akku-u vimudrama hūṃ*. *a se su mahilāvara ra-aṇaḥ*, for the sake of the good cause, *su vu i mu visesu sarvacchu ra a la sa rantā*. *takkara aṇu vidhamahilā vara ra*.
"O subtle one, pure arms! O you who have well risen from the syllable *mu*!
By chanting this, the *Sarvarājyasamāyogaḍākinījālasamvara* is accomplished; there is no doubt in this. (126)
The Knowledge of the Seal of the Glorious Vajrasūrya.
That very Blessed One, the yoga of Vajrasattva Tathāgata, is established as the glorious Saptimudrā for the purification of Haṭhayoga. ||127||
Having attained mastery through the liberation of all-purity, he should crush all worlds by means of his valorous assault. 128.

Toward passionate women, he may indeed be passionate; toward the wicked, he is truly wicked; toward the gentle, he becomes gentle; and toward those who are fierce and violent, he becomes fierce and violent. 129.
Four-faced, four-armed, four-legged, and four-handed, the great king Hayagrīva, the Supreme Lord, attains perfection. 130.
The glorious one holds a universal lotus with his left hand in the *khaṭaka* gesture, while with his right hand in the triple-bannered gesture he utters, "Arise, O Siddhi! along with the vajra. 131.
Having sealed [them] with this mudrā, one should raise up even those who have fallen utterly, and in an instant, bring all under the command of "Arise! (Sarvottiṣṭhā). ||132||
The mudrā named Subhagaśrīvajrotthāna, which is the union of all accomplishments.

By means of the yoga of the right and left [feet], through the application of the pratyālīḍha posture, and having assumed the wrathful cross-legged posture (krodhaparyaṅka), one should crush all worlds. ||133||
The mudrā named Śrīvajrakrodhāsana.
Now, I shall specifically proclaim the Śrīparaśvasaṅgīta, which accomplishes all activities for this knowledge of mudrās. 134.

He whose form and appearance grant more bliss than a thousand Madanas, yet who is terrifying to those with sensual desires because he subdues them through his discipline—surpassing even a thousand Yamas in his power. 135.
Furthermore, with a gentle form, he is more than a thousand times greater than Brahmā;
within the supreme mandala of all, all the Tathāgatas attain accomplishment for me. (136)
Through the resolute convictions of universal purity, and by means of the forceful subduing of all adversaries, *hīḥ hi hi hi hi hīḥ*, O Supreme Lord! crush, crush all! 137.
Having assailed the Supreme Lord with repeated attacks of force and prowess, and having manifested the perfection of the Three-Eyed One again and again, the Great Yoga exclaims: "Hulu 2! ||138||
Having assailed Nārāyaṇa with persistent force, power, and prowess, the union of wrath has repeatedly torn Fortune from his heart. 139.
Having assailed Brahmā with attacks of force, power, and prowess, those who are resolute manifest liberation; thus is the union with the Remembrance (Smara) revealed.
Having seized Surateśvara through the forceful advances of passionate power and prowess, one should repeatedly strike at the waist of the all-pervading self with cries of "a la la la la hoḥ. 140.

The union [is for the sake] of uplifting beings who are extremely wicked, fierce, and violent. A la la la la hoḥ! May the supreme scripture be accomplished! Oṃ śumbhaniśumbha hūṃ phaṭ! Kapyā-kapya parikhaṇḍa u-jāhi priyamāṇḍa (ṇu) su-jā-u! Taṃ puṇḍaṇa hu vilalima oṃ!
In that regard, there is sweet speech; it is the beginning of the manifestation born from the discernment of what is to be done and what is not to be done.
That is the beginning of the manifestation; one should meditate upon that very beginning within the subtle essences (*sudravīṣu*).
By means of this which is being sung, success is attained; of this there is no doubt.
The Śrīparamāśvasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasaṃvara. ||141|| Thus.
The knowledge of the Sarvodaya mudrā.
Having entwined the index finger with the thumb, and the thumb with the index finger, this is the Śrīsiddhalocanā mudrā, characterized by the well-extended index finger. 142.
Having formed the vajra-añjali mudrā with both vajra-eyes joined together in a hollowed cup, the illustrious Vajralocanā is accomplished. 143.
By this, buddhahood itself, as well as universal sovereignty and the state of a holder of all vajras, is accomplished in this very life. (144)

The illustrious Buddhalocanā is accomplished as the one who brings all sentient beings under her control, through the accomplishments of all possible attainments and the success in the swift performance of activities. 145.
Having formed the vajra-añjali with her body slightly contracted, the fingers joined at their tips with the thumbs meeting, she is the supreme syllable. 146.
When protection has been performed by means of this [mantra] which has entered into all the joints, it is known as that which accomplishes the complete and total siddhis of the Buddhas. 147.
The seal of all eight [auspicious] symbols.
With the two vajra-añjali hands opened upward, her body slightly contracted,
with two thumbs forming formidable fangs, the fierce Vajrayakṣiṇī accomplishes the devouring of Māra and the like, as well as the transformation into a *kaṃvilī*. 148.
From that, there is the accomplishment of all penetrations and the means for supernatural knowledge;
likewise, the extraction of hidden treasures and the seizing of all one's possessions. ||149||

By means of this [practice], one swiftly achieves the subjugation of Śrī Vaiśravaṇa, the crushing of Śrī herself, the treading upon the servants (kiṃkaras), the slaying of yakṣiṇīs, and the leadership of the yakṣa hosts. 150.
The mudrā of Śrīvajrayakṣa.
By forming the vajrāñjali with the middle fingers held straight, it becomes perfected;
its two thumbs form four petals, like a pure, fully blossomed lotus. 151.
By this one is purified of sins; through the purification of sin, one awakens.
Having fully awakened to the enlightenment of the Buddhas, one attains the state of Vajrasattva. 152.
The mudrā of the illustrious Padmarāja.
Having formed the vajrāñjali with the tips of the index fingers bent outward and the thumbs [pressed against them], this is the Vajrāsana; it is also called the Śrīvajramaṇi. ||153||
By sealing with this mudrā, one achieves mastery over all the kalās;
he enjoys all excellent jewels, beginning with those that fill the sky, as well as all states of being.
Having formed the vajra-añjali, there is no confusion regarding the ministers. 154.

By means of this mudrā, which possesses the beauty of a slightly contracted [posture] or is supremely white, one attains perfection; having sealed with it, one should manifest the awakening of a Buddha. 155.
How much more so, then, for all kings, the knowledge of the pledge-mudrās (samayamudrā) that brings divine and human fortune and excellence?
The vajra of body, speech, and mind, endowed with the symbolic mudrās, through yoga becomes the arising of all; one should oneself become one's own tutelary deity. 156.
Through these, the state of all Buddhas, the state of all Heroes, and the state of all Vajra-holders are accomplished in this very life. (157)

Bowing down, [I offer praise to] those noble and exalted ones who are equal to the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), as limitless as the realm of space, and who are the accomplishments of the very self of all Buddhas. 158.
"If that which is desired is not accomplished, and if it indeed does not prosper,
[it is because one has failed in] the *Sarvabuddhasamāyoga-Ḍākinījālasamvara*.
Thus ends the knowledge of the great pledge-seal (*mahāsamayamudrā*).
One should effortlessly cause the all-pervading self, which has arisen according to its natural state in union with Śrī Vajrasattva, to enter into the all-pervading self. 160.
By means of this mudrā, the yogin falls when he wishes to fly up;
as the king who embodies all Buddhas, Vajrasattva, he attains accomplishment. 161.
